does: Pours beaten egg in a thin stream into a gently moving hot soup so that it sets in fine, silky ribbons.
how: Thicken the soup a little first; the ribbons hang better in it.
Beat the eggs well, without froth.
Bring the soup to a bare simmer and stir it in a slow circle.
Pour the egg in a thin stream from a little height, along the swirl.
Leave the soup still for a moment before stirring, so the ribbons set.

cues.text: Fine, pale yellow ribbons and flowers floating through the soup.

mistakes.mistake: Pouring the egg into a soup that is boiling hard, which breaks it into grainy bits.
mistakes.fix: Lower the heat until it barely bubbles.

mistakes.mistake: Stirring as soon as the egg goes in.
mistakes.fix: Wait a moment for the ribbons to set before you stir.
